newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Jiang to attend HK handover ceremony - paper.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiang to attend HK handover ceremony - paper.

text.p: Chinese president Jiang Zemin will come to Hong Kong on June 30 to attend the ceremony marking the historic handover of the British colony to China, a Hong Kong newspaper said on Tuesday.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of colonial rule.
A glitzy ceremony, attended by 4,000 dignitaries, will be staged by Britain and China to mark the sovereignty transfer.

The independent Chinese-language Ming Pao newspaper quoted sources in Beijing as saying Jiang would be accompanied by Chinese Premier Li Peng, National People's Congress Standing Committee chairman Qiao Shi and Central Military Commission vice-chairman Liu Huaquing.
Jiang would also attend the swearing-in ceremony of the new Hong Kong government in the early hours of July 1, the newspaper said.

However, it said both Jiang and Li would have to return to the Chinese capital on that same day for a state banquet attended by 3,500 guests at Great Hall of People. Britain's heir to the throne Prince Charles will lead the British delegation at the handover ceremony. United States Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan and VIPs from 40 countries have been invited to the handover party.
